sentences.text:
Present second bail application under Section 483 BNSS on behalf of the applicant Vishu Tomar,
has been filed seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 771 of 2024 under Section 103 (1) and 238 BNS, Police Station-Baraut, District Baghpat, during the pendency of the trial before the Court below.
Ist bail application of the applicant before this Court was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file fresh bail application vide order dated 19.09.2025.

The bail application of the applicant before the Court below was rejected by the learned Sessions Judge, Baghpat, vide order dated 06.02.205 and the applicant is incarcerated in jail since 13.11.2024.
Shri Sunil Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant vehemently argued that the applicant is entirely innocent and has been falsely roped in this very case crime number for alterior motive.

The First Information Report giving rise to the present case crime number has been lodged nominating the applicant and 2 other persons and one unknown person alleging that the son of the informant namely Sunny Tomar was picked up from his house in the night of 11/12.11.2024 by the accused persons including the applicant in a Swift Dzire Car, taken to a wine shop, administered wine,
murdered and left abandoned near the divider of the newly constructed Delhi-Dehradoon Express Way.
Learned counsel has made four fold arguments in support of the bail plea.

It is contended that as per the allegations in the First Information Report all the accused persons are stated to have arrived at the house of the son of the informant namely Sunny and took him away along with them in the Swift Dzire Car.
The informant did not claim himself to be the witness of the incident.

Thereafter, the accused persons are alleged to have taken Sunny to the wine shop, purchased wine and thereafter alleged to have committed the murder of Sunny and dumped his body near the Divider of the Delhi Dehradoon Express Way.
The informant has not seen the incident.
The statement of Satendra Tomar and Harendra Tomar cannot be relied upon as the said witnesses are real brothers of the deceased Sunny and thus interested witnesses.

It is also argued that the arrest of the applicant is illegal and the recovery of articles including the passport size photo of the deceased Sunny, blood stained sleeper, Danda from the possession and pointing out of the applicant is not supported by any public or independent witness and no compliance of Section 105 BNSS has been made.

It is also argued that the applicant has been assigned the role of causing injuries to the deceased by a Danda and the injuries sustained by the deceased could not have been caused by the weapon assigned to the applicant.
Criminal history of one other case i.e. Case Crime No. 808 of 2020 under Section 363, 376 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station-Baraut, District-Bagpat has been explained in para 23 of the affidavit.
The charge sheet in the present case has also been filed on 01.12.2024 but the trial has yet not commenced.
There is no direct, indirect or otherwise any evidence against the applicant.
The applicant undertakes to cooperate in the trial and not misuse the liberty of bail if granted.
Bail is accordingly prayed for.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail plea by submitting that the applicant is the main accused and the deceased Sunny was done to death brutally.

He has invited the attention of the Court to the injury report which reflects as many as 16 injuries including the injury no.

sentences.text: The alleged Danda used by the applicant in the commission of crime with blood stains has also been recovered from the possession and pointing out of the applicant.
It is accordingly prayed that the bail application warrants rejection.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, nature of allegations,
heinousness of offence of murder and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, the Court is of the opinion that it is not a fit case for bail.
Hence, this bail application is hereby rejected.

(Ashutosh Srivastava,J.) November 6, 2025 Deepak/
